examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Limit Using L'Hopital's Rule Twice
examples.worked_solution:
If we plug in $x=0$ we get the indeterminate form $\dfrac{0}{0},$ so  we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\eqalign{
\lim_{x\to0}  \dfrac{\sin^2 (2x)}{x^2} &= \lim_{x\to 0}  \dfrac {\left[\sin^2 (2x)\right]'}{[x^2]'}\[5pt]
&= \lim_{x\to 0}  \dfrac{2\cdot \sin (2x) \cdot\cos (2x)\cdot 2}{2x}\[5pt]
&= \lim_{x\to 0}{2\cos (2x)} \cdot \lim_{x\to 0} \dfrac{\sin (2x)}{x}\[5pt]
&= 2\cos(2\cdot 0)\lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\sin (2x)}{x}\[5pt]
&= 2\lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\sin (2x)}{x}
}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\dfrac{0}{0}.$ But that's okay, because we can just apply L'Hopital's rule again! We get

$$
\eqalign{
\lim_{x\to0}  \dfrac{\sin^2 (2x)}{x^2} &= 2\lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\sin (2x)}{x}\[5pt]
&=  2\lim_{x\to0}  \dfrac {[\sin (2x)]'}{[x]'}\[5pt]
&=  2\lim_{x\to0}  \dfrac {2\cos (2x)}{1}\[5pt]
&= 4\cos(2\cdot 0)\
&=4.
}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Note that plugging in $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ However, we can use L'Hopital's rule to find this limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \pi /4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡2x} & ={lim}_{x\to \pi /4}\frac{[\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x]^{′}}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡2x]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \pi /4}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})}{-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})}{-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =\frac{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}{-2(1)} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
